I’m 65 years old, and I’ve farmed my 8 mu in Quzhou County since I was a boy. My middle-school education means I can read the numbers on a seed bag and follow what the extension agent says, but the truth is I trust my own eyes and what my neighbors do more than any book. I’ve had good years and bad years, and at my age I don’t gamble.

The wheat is already in the ground on 6 mu — I planted it last October with the same improved variety I’ve used for five years, the one that got through that late freeze in 2018 when my cousin lost half his stand. I put down about 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and I’ll topdress with urea when it greens up and again at jointing. The extension fellow says 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but I’ve always done closer to 16 kg N per mu, plus about 7 kg each of phosphorus and potassium. Better to spend a few extra yuan than to risk a thin stand — I remember 2002, and I’m not going through that again. I’ll irrigate three times if the spring stays dry, and spray three times for weeds and aphids when I see them. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather holds.

After the wheat comes off in early June, I’ve got maybe a week before the maize has to go in. I’ll use the no-tillage planter straight into the wheat stubble — no time for ploughing, and the soil moisture is too precious to disturb. Hybrid seed, the kind everyone uses now. I’ll put about 15 kg N per mu total, split between base fertilizer with the planter and a topdress at the big trumpet stage, plus 6 kg each of P and K. Two irrigations, maybe three if July is a furnace. Two pesticide sprays for borers and weeds. I’m hoping for 520 kg per mu.

The other 2 mu near the house I’m keeping in cotton. I know — at my age the picking is hard on my back and my wife complains every autumn. But that ground is light and sandy, and it’s grown cotton as long as I can remember. I’ve cut back from what I used to plant, but 2 mu we can still manage between us, especially since the hybrid Bt cotton means fewer bollworm sprays. I’ll rotary till in April, lay the plastic mulch, and put down lighter fertilizer — about 12 kg N per mu, 4 kg P, 4 kg K. Two irrigations at flowering and boll filling, three pesticide applications total. If I get 280 kg per mu of seed cotton I’ll be satisfied. I thought about peanuts or vegetables, but vegetables need constant babysitting and the market jumps around. Cotton I understand. Wheat and corn I understand. At 65, I stick with what I know.
